request.system: You are clustering code review findings from one PR. Always respond with valid JSON.
request.prompt:
You are clustering code review findings from the same PR. For each PAIR below, decide whether the two findings describe the SAME underlying issue — same root cause in the same code location. Different wording is fine. A finding about a DIFFERENT defect in the same file or function is NOT the same issue. Severity or aspect differences of the same root cause ARE the same issue.


For THIS scoring pass, duplicate equivalence is stricter than sharing a root cause.
You must compare the COMPLETE MATERIAL CLAIMS, including mechanism, triggering
conditions, execution path, and consequence. The same line or broad concern does
not establish equivalence. A report of wrong-category selection, a case/rename
mismatch, a crash, and a silent fallback are different claims even at one lookup.
An inactive/unbound API concern and an alleged active user-facing failure differ.
A compound report with an additional material claim does NOT equal its subset.
Differences only in wording, severity, or hedging do not create separate claims.
If the claimed mechanisms, triggers or consequences conflict, or one report adds
an unsupported/different material factual claim, return same=false. You are NOT
verifying which claim is true; do not repair or reinterpret either report to make
them match. If unsure whether their full claims are equivalent, return false.

For every numbered pair, extract what A and B actually CLAIM into mechanism,
trigger and consequence. Then list material_differences and give your equivalence
verdict, confidence and reason. same=true requires no material differences.
Return ONLY this JSON object, with EVERY pair index exactly once:
{"pairs":[{"pair":1,"a":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"b":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"material_differences":[],"same":true,"confidence":0.9,"reason":"..."}]}

PAIR 15:
A: isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner are awaited sequentially and are redundant — if the intent is admin-or-owner, isTeamAdmin subsumes owner in every sane role hierarchy, making one of the two calls dead work. Two sequential DB round-trips on every addGuests request where one would do, and the redundant pair is exactly what allowed the && operator bug to hide.
B: Redundant double DB calls: the `&&` condition evaluates both isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner when a single check would suffice (addGuests.handler.ts:45-47)

PAIR 16:
A: isTeamAdminOrOwner computes (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)), requiring the caller to be BOTH admin AND owner rather than either, so plain team admins are denied. A team admin who is not the team owner attempts to add guests to a team booking they do not organize and receives FORBIDDEN despite being an admin — the authorization gate silently rejects a class of users the UI's add_members menu item is shown to.
B: The permission check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && instead of ||, so a user must be BOTH team admin AND owner to qualify, silently stripping the intended 'team admin or owner can add guests' permission from real admins and owners. A team admin (or owner who is not admin) who is neither the organizer nor an attendee of a booking gets FORBIDDEN 'you_do_not_have_permission' when adding guests, contradicting the accepted requirement that team admins/owners can manage guests on their team's bookings.

PAIR 17:
A: isTeamAdminOrOwner computes (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)), requiring the caller to be BOTH admin AND owner rather than either, so plain team admins are denied. A team admin who is not the team owner attempts to add guests to a team booking they do not organize and receives FORBIDDEN despite being an admin — the authorization gate silently rejects a class of users the UI's add_members menu item is shown to.
B: The team permission gate uses `&&`, requiring the user to be BOTH admin and owner simultaneously, contradicting the variable's own name `isTeamAdminOrOwner`. A team admin who is not an owner (and any owner, if isTeamAdmin excludes the OWNER role) selects 'additional_guests' on a team booking and receives FORBIDDEN you_do_not_have_permission, silently breaking the feature for exactly the roles the code claims to grant.

PAIR 18:
A: isTeamAdminOrOwner computes (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)), requiring the caller to be BOTH admin AND owner rather than either, so plain team admins are denied. A team admin who is not the team owner attempts to add guests to a team booking they do not organize and receives FORBIDDEN despite being an admin — the authorization gate silently rejects a class of users the UI's add_members menu item is shown to.
B: The team-staff permission check joins isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with '&&' even though the variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner; since a team membership holds a single role, the admin-or-owner grant collapses to owner-only (or to nothing, if isTeamAdmin excludes OWNER). A team ADMIN who is not the booking's organizer and not an attendee receives FORBIDDEN when adding guests to their team's booking; the feature's access objective was silently narrowed from 'admins or owners' to 'owners only', and both membership queries always execute even when the first is false.

PAIR 19:
A: isTeamAdminOrOwner computes (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)), requiring the caller to be BOTH admin AND owner rather than either, so plain team admins are denied. A team admin who is not the team owner attempts to add guests to a team booking they do not organize and receives FORBIDDEN despite being an admin — the authorization gate silently rejects a class of users the UI's add_members menu item is shown to.
B: In addGuests.handler.ts:46-48, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` (isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)) where the intent — and the variable name — requires `||`; since owners are a subset of admins in the role model, the gate collapses to owner-only and non-owner team admins get FORBIDDEN on a normal, intended flow.

PAIR 20:
A: isTeamAdminOrOwner computes (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)), requiring the caller to be BOTH admin AND owner rather than either, so plain team admins are denied. A team admin who is not the team owner attempts to add guests to a team booking they do not organize and receives FORBIDDEN despite being an admin — the authorization gate silently rejects a class of users the UI's add_members menu item is shown to.
B: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — (P2, conf 75) `const isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` requires a user to be both admin AND owner, so team ADMINs (who see team bookings in the list and get the "Add guests" entry point at BookingListItem.tsx:194 with no permission gating) click it and always receive FORBIDDEN "you_do_not_have_permission" -- the UI entry point is shown to users who cannot use it.
